name: Mercer Union
known: Langer and the gallery's director were first charged under the Criminal Code's child pornography provisions, the Crown withdrew those charges and prosecuted the paintings instead, and the works were later ruled legal.

name: The Power Plant Contemporary Art Gallery
known: It is a registered charity under the legal name The Art Gallery at Harbourfront, operating as The Power Plant, run by a board of directors (annual report).
Leadership: CEO Carolyn Vesely and artistic director Adelina Vlas as of 31 March 2026 (annual report 2025-26).

TD Bank Group and its TD Ready Commitment sponsored touring exhibitions by Manuel Mathieu, Sasha Huber, Shona Illingworth and Nathan Eugene Carson (annual report 2023-24); the 2025-26 report lists a TD Curatorial Fellow for 2025-27.
Board: Katrina Rempel of BMO Capital Markets and Julia Park of CIBC (treasurer) sit on the board of 14 directors (the gallery's leadership page).
TD funds a TD Curatorial Fellow for 2025 to 2026.

name: YYZ Artists' Outlet
known: Managed by a volunteer board of directors and curated by consensus (stated by YYZ).

name: Arthur Erickson House and Garden
known: On site: guided garden tours only, and the Foundation is set to restore the 860-square-foot house under a conservation plan (aefoundation.ca, Globe and Mail).
Lambert chairs a board of 16 directors (aefoundation.ca/governance).
Names its directors and patrons on its governance page and gives its charity number, 888354842RR0001, on its donate page.
Phyllis Lambert chairs a board of 16 directors.

name: Artspeak
known: Mandate: "to exhibit contemporary art and to encourage a dialogue between visual art and writing" (Artspeak director/curator job listing, 2022).
Directors: Lorna Brown was director-curator from 1999 to 2004 (Wikipedia).
Canadian Art, 15 March 2017, quotes the curator Tarah Hogue on Bopha Chhay's "recent appointment as director of Artspeak".

The 2022 director/curator listing says the post includes successful grant applications to municipal, provincial and federal governments, foundations and other private sources, and pays $56,000 a year plus benefits (Akimbo).

name: Contemporary Art Gallery (CAG)
known: Matthew Hyland is Executive Director.
The staff page lists a "TD Assistant Curator of Programming"; the page does not say who pays for the post.

name: Western Front
known: Named for the building's pioneer-style facade, its West Coast location and the founders' avant-garde pursuits, according to the centre's own history page.

Director Caitlin Jones told the Georgia Straight (6 January 2016): "it's deeply ironic that we are securing our own stability." The centre had held "Urgent Imagination" in autumn 2015, a conference and exhibition that explored housing and space affordability and critiqued developer-driven planning (

name: grunt gallery
known: The grant will pay off its mortgage and supply $240,000 towards purchasing a new facility; program director Glenn Alteen thanked RIZE and the City of Vancouver (grunt press release).

name: Art Gallery of Greater Victoria
known: In 2016 the chairman of Polygon Homes, Michael Audain, pledged C$2 million through the Audain Foundation toward a C$24 million redevelopment that was contingent on C$14 million from the federal and provincial governments (Citified).
The 2023-24 annual report (archived copy) names Carol Anne Harper as board president and Nancy Noble as director and CEO.
The gallery posts annual and financial reports for 2022/23 to 2024/25, names its 2026/27 directors, and shows sponsor logos in giving tiers with no date.

name: Audain Art Museum
known: Founded by Michael Audain and Yoshiko Karasawa to house British Columbia works from their private collection.
Named for Michael Audain, who is chairman and major shareholder of the home builder Polygon Homes (Wikipedia).

The museum was founded to house works from the founders' private collection; the museum's page says memberships and donations support its programmes, and credits the Audain Foundation with funding at least one artwork (stated by the museum).
Audain Foundation (founded 1997, chaired by Audain) funds British Columbia visual arts and sponsors the $100,000 Audain Prize for the Visual Arts (Wikipedia).

Audain is chairman and major shareholder of Polygon Homes, which he joined in 1980 and which with its affiliate Morningstar Homes has completed over 34,000 homes in Metro Vancouver (Wikipedia, Michael Audain page).
Posts four annual reports (2020-21 to 2023-24) on Issuu, lists 18 trustees; names endowment founders by giving tier.

name: Plug In ICA
known: Lorraine Raboud and Suzanne Gillies were the founding directors (plugin.org/history;

name: Urban Shaman Contemporary Aboriginal Art
known: Staff named on the site include Artistic Director Justin Bear L'Arrivée and Operations Director Debbie Keeper.
The Staff and Board page names three directors: Louis Ogemah (president), Riva Symko and Albert McLeod.
The site names three directors and shows nine undated, unlabelled supporter logos.

name: Winnipeg Art Gallery-Qaumajuq
known: Its inaugural Qaumajuq exhibition, Inua, was organised by Inuit curators and showed more than 90 contemporary Inuit artists (The Art Newspaper, ArtReview).
Ferdinand Eckhardt served as a director of the gallery from 1953 to 1974 (Global News, The Canadian Press).

name: Bienal de Artes Mediales de Santiago
known: The 17th edition, "Hiperrealidades", ran from 9 to 26 October 2025, curated by the artist Nicolás Oyarce Carrión, with its listed events at the Centro Cultural Gabriela Mistral (GAM), Av.
It took its current name with the 11th edition in 2013, when Enrique Rivera became director.
Directorate: Luz María Sorolla (Secretaria General), Valentina Montero (Vicepresidenta) and Manuela Ossa (Tesorera);
Catalina Ossa is Executive Director.
Its organiser CChV posts annual reports for 2018 to 2025, yearly balance sheets, a statement of its two public funding programmes, and its directorate.

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago
known: Daniel Cruz Valenzuela, a visual artist and University of Chile academic, became director on 15 May 2021, succeeding Francisco Brugnoli, who led the museum for 23 years (University of Chile news, 17 May 2021).
Director Daniel Cruz called the museum's financing "terrible" in 2021 and said repairing the roofs costs about 180 million pesos.
